nodes.title: Reject input that is not a string
nodes.why: The contract says strings only, so a clear TypeError beats a confusing result for null or an array.
nodes.alternative: Coerce the input with String(s) and keep going.
nodes.tradeoff: Strict input checking surfaces caller bugs early; coercion would hide them.

nodes.title: Push the closer each opener expects
nodes.why: Storing the closer, not the opener, turns the later check into a single equality test.
nodes.alternative: Push the opener and look up its partner when a closer arrives.
nodes.tradeoff: One lookup at push time instead of one at pop time; the stack reads as a list of promises.

nodes.title: Fail on the first closer that does not match
nodes.why: The most recent unmatched opener must close first; an empty stack pops undefined, so a stray closer fails the same way.
nodes.tradeoff: Counters miss order errors such as "([)]"; the stack catches them in one pass.

nodes.title: Valid only when nothing is left open
nodes.why: Reaching the end with pending closers means some opener was never closed.
nodes.alternative: Return true as soon as the loop finishes without a mismatch.
nodes.tradeoff: One final length check covers "(" and "(()" without extra cases.

nodes.title: Drop every character that is not a bracket
nodes.why: Pair removal only works when brackets sit next to each other, so other text has to go first.
nodes.tradeoff: One extra pass over the input keeps the removal loop simple.

nodes.title: Remove adjacent matching pairs
nodes.why: A valid string always contains at least one adjacent pair, and removing it leaves a valid string.
nodes.alternative: Keep a stack of expected closers.
nodes.tradeoff: Easy to explain, but each pass rescans the string, so deep nesting costs O(n²).

nodes.title: Stop when a pass removes nothing
nodes.why: If no pair was removed, no further pass can remove one either.
nodes.alternative: Loop a fixed number of times based on the length.
nodes.tradeoff: The fixed-point check ends as early as possible without guessing an iteration count.

nodes.title: Valid only when nothing is left
nodes.why: Any bracket that survives every pass has no partner in the right position.
nodes.alternative: Compare the counts of openers and closers.
nodes.tradeoff: Equal counts are not enough for "([)]"; an empty remainder is.
